note: R0 adopts nothing permanently: 'adopt-as-r3-input' means the worktree draft file is registered as the starting point for R3, not merged, staged or committed. Every verdict below is backed by code read statically plus the CPU-only test runs recorded in verification.json.

decisions.rationale: Plan §5.1/§5.3 requires the Backend protocol to expose artifact_builder() and to have no compile/compile_all hook. The draft removes both methods from the Protocol and adds artifact_builder(kernel_contract, math, kernel_names), so the only way to obtain a builder is the factory the plan mandates.
evidence: AST/grep: after the draft the only remaining `def compile(`/`def compile_all(` in the tree are the runtime primitives tcenv/backends/metal/runtime.py::MetalContext.compile and ::MetalContext.compile_all plus two test stubs; no Backend implementation keeps the removed hook.
Plan §2.1 row 3 lists Backend.compile/compile_all as an R3 deletion; this draft performs exactly that deletion and nothing else on the protocol.
r3_requirements: Keep the factory as the only entry; R3 must not re-add a convenience compile wrapper for any caller.
R3 must add the structural check that no Backend subclass defines compile/compile_all, by AST rather than by hasattr only.

decisions.rationale: The Metal backend becomes a pure factory returning MetalSourceBuilder configured with the contract, math mode and declared kernel names. That matches §5.1 (factory takes Specialization + candidate math/names, no shell/path/command).
evidence: The factory passes only kernel_contract/math/kernel_names into MetalSourceBuilder; it accepts no arbitrary command, path or build string.
tests/support/npu_sim/fake_backend.py migrates the only other Backend implementation to the same shape, so the protocol change is not Metal-only in practice.
r3_requirements: R1 gives the factory the registered LoweringProfile name; R3 must keep the factory from recomputing lowering configuration.
R3 must prove the factory is reached from evaluate/xcworker/probes/profile/fill (spy on backend.artifact_builder), not a directly constructed builder.

symbols: native descriptor kernel_names/kernels for multi-stage builds
decisions.rationale: These parts concentrate the source→pipeline call in one builder method and let one build own a multi-stage pipeline set, which is what §5.1/§5.2 want. The same file also adds MetalSourceBuilder.compile_source, which is discarded (D-D3).
evidence: _compile_assembled is the only place in the builder that calls MetalContext.compile/compile_all; §5.2 makes MetalSourceBuilder._compile_assembled the sole legitimate owner of those calls.

tcenv/backends/metal/runtime.py::MetalContext.compile_all calls self.compile for the first name, so the draft's 1-name branch (context.compile) and the multi-name branch (context.compile_all) are behaviourally the same call sequence.

candidate_sha256 is unaffected: SourceBundle carries the candidate bytes and build() assembles the contract header internally, so provenance.source_sha256 stays the candidate text (F-3 / §3 identity table).
r3_requirements: Delete MetalSourceBuilder.compile_source (D-D3) so the primitive has exactly one caller inside the builder.
Replace the MetalKernelSet + getattr(handle, 'kernels') convention with an explicit typed handle-set contract in the neutral model; do not keep two handle vocabularies.

Add the §5.1 BuildError attachments (typed BuildProvenance with artifact_set_digest=null, assembled_sha256) at the compile-failure site; the draft sets report_detail but attaches no provenance (see X-2).
Move the typed profile acquisition ahead of any candidate-level compile judgement (non-UTF-8 path, X-1).

decisions.rationale: _evaluate_in_process stops calling backend.assemble/compile/compile_all and instead asks the backend for its builder and calls build(). The compile_error report text keeps its pre-refactor shape (rewritten diagnostic only) and the candidate bytes remain the SOURCE artifact.
evidence: The builder receives SourceBundle(kernel_source.encode('utf-8')) and task_contract=contract; the contract header is assembled inside build(), so candidate_sha256 still describes exactly what the model wrote.
Only BuildError(error_class='compile') is mapped to status=compile_error; other classes are re-raised, matching the legacy 'toolchain failures are not candidate failures' rule (§5.3 item 4).
The report keeps rep.compile = {ok: False, errors: ...} with rewrite_compiler_lines applied inside the builder, i.e. the same text as HEAD's evaluate path.
r3_requirements: Keep exactly one build() call per candidate and use BuildOutcome.executable_handles() only for local handles.
Map BuildError(deadline) to timeout before any crash path if a local deadline is ever introduced (§5.3 item 3); today local callers pass no deadline.
Pass deadline_monotonic=None explicitly at every local call site (R3 spy assertion).

decisions.rationale: Profiling used to compile through ctx.compile/ctx.compile_all, i.e. a second source→pipeline path. The draft routes it through the same factory and build(), keeps the multi-stage ordering from the parsed taic-launch spec, and stops calling assemble itself.
evidence: After the draft xcworker.py contains no ctx.compile/ctx.compile_all and builds the name list from spec.stages, matching what evaluate.py passes to the builder.
The multi-stage launch is still one build; by_name ordering is preserved for stage execution.
r3_requirements: R3 must spy backend.artifact_builder -> build for the profiling path and assert one outcome for the multi-stage launch.

decisions.rationale: report_detail separates the builder-facing classification message from the report diagnostic text, which is needed to keep the local compile_error text byte-identical. The live-handle invariant closes a real hole: two records that both omit the handle compare equal only because the handle is excluded from equality and digests.
evidence: BuildOutcome.__post_init__ now rejects an outcome whose evidence.native and bundle.native both carry handle=None, so a handle-less 'success' cannot be constructed.
tests/backends/metal/test_source_builder.py::test_one_build_outcome_must_name_one_live_executable extends the existing invariant test with the both-None case.
executable_handles() is the single unwrap point used by evaluate.py and xcworker.py.
r3_requirements: Replace the getattr(handle, 'kernels') heuristic with an explicit handle-set contract (X-3); a duck-typed convention is a second vocabulary.
Keep BuildError as the failure attachment; do not add a second outcome DTO (§2.1 row 11).

decisions.rationale: The test file follows the protocol change: the legacy comparison now calls the runtime primitive directly (ctx.compile) instead of the deleted backend hook, and the stub backends grow a compile method on the context. Placement is correct (tests/backends/metal).
evidence: The file lives under tests/backends/metal and imports tcenv.backends.metal, which satisfies tests/README.md layering.
The CPU-only subset of this file passes in the adopted-subset replay (verification.json / V-4).
r3_requirements: Add the builder-conformance check from §5.1 (every registered builder that can produce a candidate report must attach typed provenance on compile errors) and the AST/call-graph checks from §5.3.1.

decisions.rationale: The fake evaluator backend must implement the same single entry point as the real one, otherwise remote/simulated paths silently keep a second compile hook. The fake builder produces a neutral BuildOutcome with a fake live handle, which is the shape §6.3 describes for simulators.
evidence: FakeNpuBackend no longer defines compile/compile_all and returns _FakeSourceBuilder from artifact_builder.
The fake handle set uses a dataclass with a kernels attribute, mirroring MetalKernelSet, so the same unwrap path is exercised on CPU tests.
r3_requirements: Give the fake a compile-failure path that attaches provenance, or declare it source_only/simulator in R4 so the §5.1 conformance check can exempt it explicitly (X-8).
R4 must register build_kind for builder_id fake-npu-builder and confirm the reported build is simulator/source_only, never confirmable.

decisions.rationale: The draft replaces ctx.compile with MetalSourceBuilder().compile_source(...): it constructs a builder directly (forbidden by §5.3 item 2) and returns a bare CompiledKernel with no BuildOutcome, which is exactly the 'convenience compile' bypass §5.1 forbids. Plan §5.2 also names probes.py::_compile_probe_source as a工作树 addition to delete. Keeping the change would additionally break the registered tool manifest.
evidence: Measured: the file change invalidates backends/metal/tools/tool_impl.toml::handler_source_sha256 (registered d5c69e1f… for HEAD, worktree md5 2defe4ab…), so 13 CPU tests in tests/backends/metal/test_tool_protocol.py fail with ToolError 'handler source differs from its registered digest'; they pass on a pristine HEAD export.
MetalSourceBuilder() with backend=None constructs a new MetalBackend, i.e. the composition root bypass §5.3 item 2 calls out.
compile_source() creates a second call site for MetalContext.compile outside _compile_assembled (D-D3).
r3_requirements: Start from HEAD behaviour and implement §5.2: typed probe source/kernel name from the validated request, built through backend.artifact_builder with an independently registered diagnostic profile whose contract declares raw-source/no-task-header assemble, and keep the BuildOutcome.
If probes.py changes again, regenerate the tool manifest digest in the same change.

decisions.rationale: Same two defects as D-D1: it constructs MetalSourceBuilder directly and compiles the fixed _COPY_SRC through compile_source with no BuildOutcome, while §5.2 requires the bandwidth calibration to use an independently registered raw-source diagnostic contract/profile through the factory and to retain its BuildOutcome.
evidence: The draft's body is `builder = MetalSourceBuilder(); ... builder.compile_source(_COPY_SRC, [name])[0]` — no factory, no outcome, no provenance.
The MLX/measure_peak_flops path is untouched, so this file's diff only affects the diagnostic bandwidth line; reverting it restores HEAD behaviour exactly.
r3_requirements: Implement §5.2's registered diagnostic profile path in R3; do not reuse a task LoweringProfile for calibration.

decisions.rationale: This is the entry point plan §2.1/§5.2 requires R3 to delete: it compiles already-assembled text for a caller that holds no task contract, returns bare handles, and duplicates the primitive call that _compile_assembled already owns. Adopting it would freeze a second build vocabulary into the R3 baseline.
evidence: Only two production callers exist in the draft (probes.py::_compile_probe_source, profile.py::measure_peak_bandwidth); both are discarded here, so nothing in the adopted subset depends on compile_source.
Adopted-subset replay (V-4) removes compile_source and keeps all other adopted files, and introduces no new CPU test failures.
r3_requirements: R3 deletes compile_source; diagnostic callers use build() with a registered diagnostic profile.

decisions.rationale: The structural half is a regex text search, which plan §2.1 row 5 and §5.3 item 1 explicitly reject as proof; the GPU half imports tcenv.backends.metal inside tests/shared, which breaks tests/shared/README.md and makes tests/shared/test_structure.py::test_backend_free_tests_do_not_import_a_backend fail. Its claims are worth keeping, its form is not.
evidence: Regex scope holes (read from the file): receiver whitelist backend|ctx|context|metal_context|MetalContext misses self.compile( in tcenv/backends/metal/runtime.py::MetalContext._fill_kernel — the very bypass §5.2 still requires deleting; whole-file exclusions BUILD_PRIMITIVE_FILES hide any future call added to runtime.py/source_builder.py; the scan root is tcenv/ only, so experiments/dispatch_ab.py's direct ctx.compile call is invisible; aliases and getattr are not matched at all.

Measured: 6 AST ImportFrom hits of tcenv.backends.metal in tests/shared/test_single_build_path.py make tests/shared/test_structure.py::test_backend_free_tests_do_not_import_a_backend fail with 'shared/test_single_build_path.py:53' (triage log in verification.json).
The two GPU cases were not run and cannot run in R0 (gpu marker, explicit permission required), so they are not evidence of anything yet.
r3_requirements: Replace with AST/call-graph checks per §5.3 item 1 (aliases, delegation, getattr) plus spy assertions on backend.artifact_builder -> build.
Split placement: structural, backend-free checks may stay in tests/shared; the real-Mac evaluator cases move to tests/backends/metal and keep their gpu marker.

defects.title: non-UTF-8 candidate is classified as compile failure before a typed provenance exists
defects.detail: source_bundle.source.decode('utf-8') raises BuildError('compile', ...) before _device_info()/_profile_for(), so the only identity the failure carries is the candidate digest (no typed BuildProvenance, no assembled_sha256). Plan §5.1 and F-40 require either provenance-first ordering or a pre-build 'rejected' verdict.

defects.title: compile-failure BuildError carries no typed provenance attachment
defects.detail: The draft sets report_detail + log + duration_ms but does not attach the typed BuildProvenance/assembled_sha256 that §5.1 requires R3 to add for schema 4 partial projection. R4's partial shape cannot be produced from this failure without probing inside except.

defects.title: handle set is a duck-typed convention, not a neutral type
defects.detail: getattr(native.handle, 'kernels', None) decides whether a handle is a set. Any handle object that happens to expose kernels changes the meaning, and the neutral model gains an implicit second vocabulary.

defects.title: internal fill kernel still compiles through the runtime primitive
defects.detail: Unchanged by the draft; it calls self.compile with a fixed source and caches the pipeline, so a pipeline exists with no BuildOutcome. §5.2 requires it to be built by a builder obtained from the factory and injected, with no lazy self.compile.

defects.title: experiments tree still compiles through the runtime primitive
defects.detail: ctx.compile(full, c.kernel_name) is a direct source→pipeline call outside tcenv/. Not covered by the draft or by its regex test (which scans tcenv/ only). R3 must decide ownership: route it through a builder or declare the experiments tree out of the production surface explicitly.

defects.title: editing a registered tool handler invalidates the tool manifest digest
defects.detail: probes.py is a registered tool handler source. The draft changed it without regenerating handler_source_sha256/manifest_sha256, which fails 13 CPU tests (tests/backends/metal/test_tool_protocol.py). R0 discards the probes.py change, so HEAD's digest is valid again; any future probes.py change must regenerate the registration in the same change.

defects.title: multi-stage native descriptor grows new keys
defects.detail: The draft adds descriptor.kernel_names and descriptor.kernels when more than one pipeline is compiled. The descriptor feeds NativeExecutable.digest (canonical_digest_document, which rejects floats), so R3/R4 must keep it float-free and bounded and must not let it become a second artifact/evidence vocabulary.

defects.title: fake builder has no compile-failure path
defects.detail: _FakeSourceBuilder always succeeds, so the §5.1 builder-conformance check (every builder that can produce a candidate report must attach provenance on compile errors) would either fail or need an explicit source_only/simulator exemption. R4 must decide which, and must report build_kind for builder_id fake-npu-builder.

defects.title: report diagnostic text must stay prefix-free
defects.detail: evaluate.py writes report_detail into rep.compile['errors']; the draft keeps it equal to the rewritten compiler message with no exception-class prefix. R4 must not re-introduce a prefix when the field becomes part of schema 4, otherwise the compile diagnostics change text.
